DSROI Global (60), FLMBRI SA (30)Participants of the Disability, Sexuality and Rights Online Institute (DSROI), and the Feminist Leadership and Movement Building and Rights Institues (FLMBRI) from 2024. CREA’s DSROI is a six weeks long online course begun in 2010. The DSROI provides a study of theory and practice of the intersections of disability, gender and sexuality with a focus on perspectives from the global South. CREA's FLMBRI is a week long institue which is a residential program designed to strengthen feminist solidarity, leadership, advocacy, and strategies for building collective power for social transformation. The Institute engages feminists from across the region to build a substantive understanding of our present with all its challenges and possibilities. It interrogates concepts and structures that affect our strategies by embedding patriarchy and gender in concepts of nation, identity, religion, polity, and development. To make meaning of what feminist struggles have transformed and how new forms of patriarchy are part of existing inequalities. Both these spaces signifcantly build the capacities of participants and CREA focuses on young and strucutally excluded groups who are from various sectors but primarily from collectives of strucrtually excluded groups.

DSROI Global- CREA concluded 11th edition of the DSROI. This edition brought together around 73 participants from 30+ countries across continents, where more than half were participants with disabilities. The main objectives were to enhance understanding of the intersections of disability, gender, and sexuality among activists and foster cross-movement collaboration. The Institute was conducted over 7 weeks with a total of 5-hours of virtual sessions per week plus a self-paced asynchronous learning platform. This year we included a reading week for catching up with resources and to slow down the pace, as well as a mid-point networking session to facilitate participant connection. As always we had ensured accessibility of the space with provision of sign language interpretations, captioning and accessible resources, sensory breaks and support with internet bundles. CREA provided an interactive platform with curated resources, including disability arts. This year, we introduced an "Ask Me Anything" (AMA) session, facilitating a live chat space for participants and faculty members. We are also compiling archives of Radical Action videos from previous DSROI editions. FLMBARI S.A.- CREA conducted Feminist leadership, movement Building, and Rights Institute– South Asia which is a residential program, designed to strengthen feminist solidarity, leadership, advocacy, and strategies for building collective power for social transformation. The Institute engages feminists from across the region to build a substantive understanding of our present with all its challenges and possibilities. It interrogates concepts and structures that have a bearing on our strategies through embedding patriarchy and gender in concepts of nation, identity, religion, polity and development. To make meaning of what feminist struggles have transformed, and how new forms of patriarchy are part of existing inequalities. It was discussed that every year at the Institute there are participants from diverse backgrounds doing exceptional work. Therefore, the importance of fostering friendships and cross-border solidarities among participants can be beneficial to each of them. Crea can explore methods for building and maintaining supportive participant groups not only during the program duration but also after its culmination. A total of 28 participants attended FLMBARI SA.

FLMBaRI SA- The 2025 edition (in Colombo) was an immersive, week-long Institute that brought together 30 feminist leaders and activists from Bangladesh, India, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. It created a space for collective exploration of feminism with power, patriarchy, sexuality, nationalism, climate justice, and movement building. A core impact of the Institute was the shift in how participants understood leadership and power. Many entered the program viewing leadership through the lens of individual empowerment or representation, but left with a deeper commitment to collective, non-hierarchical, and care-based models. The Institute built intersectional and cross-border solidarity between activists working on disability rights, LGBTQIAP+ inclusion, digital accessibility, and climate action,highlighting the interconnectedness of these issues. It strengthened a network of South Asian activists committed to sustaining long-term, cross-sectoral solidarity.DSROI Global- The 12th edition (September - November 2025) saw 70 participants from over 30 countries. The cohort included a strong representation of individuals identifying as persons with disabilities. Over seven weeks, the Institute provided more than 40 hours of direct learning, along with asynchronous assignments and final project reviews. Led by a faculty of feminists with disabilities primarily from the Global South, the sessions focused on the intersections of disability, gender, and sexuality to build cross-movement solidarity. Accessibility remained a core component, featuring multiple sign language interpretations, captioning, image descriptions, internet support, and accessible learning formats. This edition also included a session on the intersections of disability justice, militarisation, conflict, and genocide.DSROI EA- Conducted over three weeks in May, the Institute brought together 34 participants, primarily feminists and disability justice activists from Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda, and Ethiopia. Co-created with a regional Advisory Group, the Institute ensured the curriculum was grounded in East African realities, covering critical intersections like legal capacity, SRHR, gender-based and ableist violence, legal capacity, and anti-gender movements. This collaborative model helped strengthen second-line leadership and reflected the lived experiences of the partners. Participants engaged in cross-country dialogues on deaf culture, cross-movement collaboration, land rights, femicide, and indigenous women with disabilities. Accessibility measures(sign language interpretation, captioning, easy-to-read materials, internet support, and sensory breaks) ensured inclusive participation.FLMBaRI EA- The 2025 FLMBaRI East Africa in Kampala brought together 30 feminist leaders including founders and directors from 11 countries across the region. Representing diverse movements from sex worker rights to disability justice, this edition’s cohort turned the seven-day residential institute into a space for reassessing leadership, power, and intersectional rights frameworks. What set FLMBaRI East Africa 2025 apart was its sense of continuity and future‑oriented collaboration. Participants left the Institute with sharper analysis, strengthened leadership, and a renewed commitment towards regional alliances.
